_readme: Genjutsu motion control (Higgsfield `hf_mult_motion_control`) is the clip maker for a sale ad built on a swipe reel: the swipe video drives ONLY the movement; the person, the room and the product come from ONE scene still we make first. Deepened 2026-10-27 from the makers' own pages and our 18 Oct learnings; same shape as gpt-image-2.5.json.

Honest gap: Higgsfield publishes no page for `hf_mult_motion_control` by that name. Its Motion Control is Kling's (Kling 3.0 Motion Control), so the maker rules below are Kling's own guide and Higgsfield's help page for it. Where a limit differs by door it is said so; every row carries its source (a URL or one of our files).
Draft: nothing here is approved. No brand, product, person or format word appears in this file.
label: Genjutsu motion control

vendor_ids.kling_motion_control: kling3_0_motion_control (mode std or pro; background_source input_image or input_video; character_orientation image or video)

limits.min_image_edge_px: 340 (Kling guide, video: short edge at least 340, long edge up to 3850); 720 on the ComfyUI door; 300 short edge on Kling's own character-image rule
limits.reference_video_seconds: 3 to 30 (Kling); 30 only when the character follows the VIDEO, 10 when it follows the IMAGE (ComfyUI, Runway)
limits.output_length: equals the reference video's length; if the motion is fast or complex it can come back shorter, never under 3 s of continuous motion extracted, and the credits are not refunded (Kling)
limits.output_shape: comes back at the stills' own shape (834x1112, 3:4, from a 4:5 still): scale it back, never crop (a crop left the original caption peeking out) (ours, 18 Oct)
limits.price_credits_per_second: Kling 3.0 Standard 9, Professional 12; Kling 2.6 Standard 5, Professional 8 (Kling's own door; Higgsfield bills in its credits)

house.aspect: 9:16 from the jump (the scene still is made 9:16, the swipe is 9:16)
house.person: the cast member's BASELINE built into a scene still (headshot, look, details, expressions); never the master (the owner, 2026-10-27)
house.orientation: video (follow the swipe's movement and camera)

inputs.name: image_references
inputs.what: The ONE scene still: the person from her baseline, standing in her room, the real product in the frame. It is both the character and the world.
inputs.allowed: one picture (jpg, png or webp, under 10 MB); whole body and head visible; arms and hands visible; room to move
inputs.we_send: the approved scene still made 9:16 on GPT Image 2.5 from the BASELINE (headshot, look, details, expressions) + her room + the real product photo; never the master, never a studio sheet

inputs.name: video_references
inputs.what: The swipe video whose movement is copied: timing, gesture, expression and (in video orientation) camera move.
inputs.allowed: one video, 3 to 30 s, mp4/mov/webm/m4v under 100 MB, short edge at least 340 px, one continuous shot, one person
inputs.we_send: the swipe's one clean shot cut on the frame map's boundaries, 9:16

inputs.name: character_orientation
inputs.what: Whether the output follows the video's orientation and camera or the still's.
inputs.allowed: video (up to 30 s; best for whole-body action) or image (up to 10 s; best for portraits with camera moves set in words)
inputs.we_send: video: the swipe's movement and camera are the point

inputs.name: mode / tier
inputs.what: Standard (about 720p) for tests, Professional (1080p) for fast hands and finer detail.
inputs.we_send: std for the first take; pro only for a shot with fast hands that failed on std

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.what: Output size tier on the Higgsfield door.

inputs.name: background_source
inputs.what: Which input gives the background: the still or the swipe video.
inputs.we_send: input_image: the room is already in our scene still, so the swipe's place never shows

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.what: Words for the background and details not covered by the motion or the still (an outfit, an added thing, the environment).
inputs.allowed: free text; the maker gives no length limit
inputs.we_send: short: keep the still's room and product, no new objects; or empty

inputs.name: keep_original_sound
inputs.what: Keep the reference video's own sound in the output.
inputs.we_send: false: the swipe's sound is not ours; voice and music are laid in at the edit

inputs.name: face reference / Element Library (Kling 3.0)
inputs.what: A separate face binding from clear close-ups (front plus side views).
inputs.allowed: facial information only; it does NOT carry clothing, hairstyle, makeup or props; binds only when the character's orientation matches the video's
inputs.we_send: not used: the face comes from the scene still

inputs.name: duration
inputs.allowed: not set by you: it follows the reference video, 3 to 30 s
inputs.we_send: the swipe shot's own length (about 2 to 5 s per shot), cut to the frame map

inputs.name: seed
inputs.allowed: not documented by the maker for this model

inputs.name: mask / region
inputs.we_send: not available: a fix is a new still or a new run

inputs.name: audio / voice reference
inputs.allowed: none: motion control copies the swipe's mouth movement, it does not take our line
inputs.we_send: not available: our line is laid under the clip at the edit

inputs.name: aspect ratio
inputs.allowed: not chosen: it follows the still; match the still's and the video's aspect (both 9:16)

structure.rule: Make the whole scene as ONE still first: the person, her room and the product in the frame. The motion model only moves what the still shows.
structure.ours: scene still on GPT Image 2.5, approved by the owner, then motion control

structure.rule: The person in the still is built from the cast BASELINE (headshot, look, details, expressions), never the master.
structure.ours: swipe_swap_job.py builds the still from c['baseline'] (headshot, look, details, expression)

structure.rule: The swipe video drives only the movement: timing, gesture, expression and camera. The person, the room and the product do not come from it.
structure.ours: video_references = the swipe shot; background_source input_image

structure.rule: Build the person inside the shot's own look (same pose, light, contact shadows, depth of field, grain); a studio sheet laid in reads as pasted on. The photo look is the swipe's, never cleaner.
structure.ours: scene still prompt carries the swipe's look

structure.rule: Match the still's framing to the video's: whole body with whole body, half body with half body, close-up with close-up. Same aspect on both.
structure.ours: still made 9:16 at the swipe's framing

structure.rule: The still must show every limb the motion needs, arms and hands included, with clear space around the body for large movement.
structure.ours: hands and arms in frame in the scene still

structure.rule: One continuous shot, one person, no cuts, camera movement or obstructions in the reference; if two people are present the larger is used. Cut the swipe at its cuts and run one shot at a time.
structure.ours: per-shot runs on the frame map's boundaries (V39)

structure.rule: Steady, moderate movement works best. Fast gestures smear in the source and again in the model: blur the source first and check fast hands in QC; use pro for a fast-hands shot.

A prop is carried only if it is in the scene still, and the maker says face binding drops props, so check the product in every clip: whole, same size, not melted. If it did not survive, the product is laid in from the real photo at the edit.
The result comes back at the still's own shape; scale it back to 9:16, never crop it.
Check the face against the baseline before a clip is kept; motion control exists because object swaps kept the original face (9 of 9 swaps kept it, 9 of 9 transfers carried ours).

Plan the blocking before the start frame: where the hands and the held props will move in the swipe. Product props sit on the side away from that path, and the motion words say for every prop the hands pass whether it stays in front of them or behind them, so nothing passes through a prop.
structure.ours: swap_bench.motion_transfer words; the start frame's product placement
structure.source: [ours] the owner, Tella review 27 Oct 2026 (AI Video Creative Feedback and Workflow Refinement)

avoid.text: Building the still from the master instead of the baseline.
A person built on a grey studio backdrop: it reads pasted on.
Cropping the stretched output: the original caption shows at the edge.
A reference video with cuts, shot changes or camera moves: it can be truncated.
Overly fast motion or a subject whose body or head is blocked.
More than one person in the reference: the largest in frame is used, not the one you meant.
Expecting our spoken line from motion control: it copies the swipe's mouth and carries no audio of ours.
Assuming a prop in the still survives the motion: the maker says face binding drops props; the product is checked in every clip and never drawn.
Under 3 s of continuous motion in the reference: the run fails and the credits are not refunded.
A close-up still with a full-body video (or the reverse), or mismatched aspect ratios.
